levels.label: Developing

item_sets.stimulus: Read the three sources about a proposal to keep the town library open on Sundays. Then answer the questions.

sources.label: Source A
sources.text:
From a town newsletter, spring issue.

Our library opened its doors on Sunday afternoons last year as a trial. Visits on Sundays averaged 340 people, more than any weekday evening. Families told volunteers that Sunday is the only day both parents are free. The council should make Sunday hours permanent.

sources.label: Source B
sources.text:
From a letter to the editor.

Sunday hours sound generous, but they are not free. Keeping the building open costs about $1,200 each Sunday in staff and heating. That money currently pays for the summer reading program, which served 900 children last year. I would rather keep the program.

sources.label: Source C
sources.text:
From a survey summary prepared by the library board.

Of 1,050 residents surveyed, 58 percent said they would use Sunday hours at least once a month. Among residents under 30, the figure was 71 percent. Only 22 percent said they had ever attended the summer reading program.
